svg.title: Pipes and Filters
svg.desc: Pipes and Filters. Split processing into independent stages connected by channels. Step 1, One big processing step: One service does every stage: slow resizing sets the pace, and it scales, deploys and fails as one. Step 2, Split into filters: Each stage becomes a filter with one job; a pipe (a queue) carries the photo to the next filter. Step 3, Scale and change one stage: Resize alone scales to 4 instances (4 × 5 = 20/s); Safety slots in, and Tag is reused for videos. Step 4, Failures and the price: Watermark crashes, so its photo is processed again; a photo that always fails is dead-lettered.

g.text: One service does every stage: slow resizing sets the pace, and it scales, deploys and fails as one.
Each stage becomes a filter with one job; a pipe (a queue) carries the photo to the next filter.
Resize alone scales to 4 instances (4 × 5 = 20/s); Safety slots in, and Tag is reused for videos.
Watermark crashes, so its photo is processed again; a photo that always fails is dead-lettered.
one deployable; process(photo) runs every stage
tag fails: retry runs it all again

g.text: Pace. Every photo waits for resizing, the slowest
Scale. 20 photos/s need 4 resizers, so you run
Change. A new watermark means testing and
Failure. When tagging fails, the retry starts over
and the costly resize runs again.
Filter: one job. It reads its input pipe, writes
its output pipe and shares nothing else.
Pipe: a queue between two filters. It holds
each photo until the next filter takes it.
Source and sinks: uploads feed the pipeline;
the catalogue and the CDN receive its output.
On its own: each filter is built, deployed and
scaled alone; only the message format is shared.
under each filter: instances × photos per second each
Backs up. 20 photos arrive each second and one
Resize does 5, so its pipe grows by 15 a second.
Scale one. Resize alone goes to 4 instances: 4 × 5 = 20
a second, and its pipe stops growing. The rest stay at 1.
Insert one. Safety goes in between Validate and
Reuse one. The same Tag filter also runs in a
Watermark crashed holding 7f3. It went back to its pipe
and only Watermark ran again, so make filters idempotent.
9c1 failed at Publish 3 times, so the broker
moved it to the dead-letter queue.
A correlation ID travels with each photo and is
logged at every hop, so one search finds them all.
• Every hop serialises the photo and stores it again.
• 6 filters and 5 pipes to deploy, scale and watch.
• Each hop adds queueing and network latency.
• No transaction spans the stages: 9c1 was resized,
watermarked and tagged, but never published.
